newsitem.title: USA: IMF official not too concerned by U.S. inflation.
newsitem.headline: IMF official not too concerned by U.S. inflation.

text.p: A senior International Monetary Fund official said on Tuesday that he was not very concerned about a possible breakout of U.S. inflation.

"It's the thing to worry about but I'm not very worried it's going to happen," IMF First Deputy Managing Director Stanley Fischer told reporters after giving a presentation to the National Economics Club.

He said that economists and policymakers were all wondering how long the United States can continue with its "very low" unemployment rates. "You can be sure they (the Federal Reserve) are watching it very carefully," he added.
The U.S. unemployment rate rose to 5.0 percent in June from a near 24-year low of 4.8 percent in May. In the past, wages have picked up and inflation has risen when unemployment has been this low.
Turning to Japan, Fischer said he did not expect the central bank there to tighten credit soon.
"I don't think there is going to be an early tightening," he said in response to a question. "There are no indications from Japanese officials of an early tightening, at least that I've seen."
